overview.text: The Mystical Supper icon depicts Christ with His disciples before His Passion. The Church’s Holy Thursday account joins this meal with the betrayal of Judas and interprets it in the setting of communion and love.
overview.reason: Necessary concise account of the named copyrighted publication; full-text reproduction permission has not been established. Traditional events and published interpretations remain attributed.

blocks.text: The displayed Last Supper was painted by Simon Ushakov in 1685 and is associated in its catalogue with Sergiev Posad. Christ and the apostles gather around the table. The complete historical image is reproduced; the icon is not labelled as a modern reconstruction of the room.

blocks.text: The OCA explains Holy Thursday through the contrast between Christ’s self-giving love and Judas’s betrayal. It describes the supper as the fulfillment of communion offered by God, set within the approaching Cross. That is the named author’s liturgical explanation, rather than an original interpretation composed for this app.

blocks.title: 1 Corinthians 11:23–26
blocks.text:
For I have received of the Lord that which also I delivered unto you, That the Lord Jesus the same night in which he was betrayed took bread:

And when he had given thanks, he brake it, and said, Take, eat: this is my body, which is broken for you: this do in remembrance of me.

After the same manner also he took the cup, when he had supped, saying, This cup is the new testament in my blood: this do ye, as oft as ye drink it, in remembrance of me.

For as often as ye eat this bread, and drink this cup, ye do shew the Lord’s death till he come.
